authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 4918 cōkṣa gives Sindhi cokho and Gujarati cokhā “cleaned rice”, alongside the pure/clean/good adjective. The survey rice forms support this semantic specialization; the underlying food sense is explicitly attested, not inferred solely from clean. Uncertain transfer between Indo-Aryan languages does not prevent this supported family link under the user’s preference.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9198.1 *bā “father” explicitly gives Nepali bā and bājyā “grandfather”. Its mother branch is separately numbered 9198.2 *bāī; sister or honorific woman senses require distinguishing other bāī families. Uncertain transfer between Indo-Aryan languages does not prevent this supported family link under the user’s preference.
